summary: Clackamas County lookout cab built 1925 on High Rock in the Mount Hood National Forest; deactivated 1964-65 and destroyed before 1970. The summit is now a public peak with views.

facts.design: Region-5 cab per register; a 1947 survey note describes a white lookout house about 12 x 12 feet on a stone foundation; a 1955 note refers to a 14 x 14 lookout house
facts.status_note: The cab was gone by 1970 (NGS recovery note). A 2020 trip report describes the summit and its view and mentions no structure.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest

access.note: Peak reached by a forest road and an unmarked trail; a 2020 trip report lists no permits or fees

visit.trail_note: About 1.12 miles round trip on a narrow forest road and an unmarked final trail; the road is drivable in a 4x4 vehicle with good clearance (2020 trip report)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives deactivation in 1964; the register and firelookout.com say the cab lasted until 1965. Both dates are stated in the story and left unresolved.
The 1947 NGS description gives about 12 by 12 feet; a 1955 NGS note refers to a 14 x 14 USFS lookout house. Left unresolved.
The Sand Mountain Society's High Rock Lookout is a different lookout in Washington's Gifford Pinchot National Forest. It is not this site and is named in the story only to separate the two.

notes_for_editor: Status 'gone' stands: the cab was destroyed before 1970 and the summit is now a peak. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced by 'public' from a 2020 trip report that lists no permits or fees; a human should confirm there is no closure. The brief's source_pages includes sandmountain.org, which describes a different High Rock Lookout in Washington (Gifford Pinchot NF, restoration in progress); that URL should come out of this record. No photos found with a usable image URL (firelookout.com credits a Fire Lookout Museum photo, not fetched). Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 7 page reads.
